hook.line: Hernando's memoir has its big moments: riots, wars, scandals that changed the city. Spanish keeps special verbs for things that do not just start, they break out.
hook.es: El Bogotazo estalló el 9 de abril de 1948.
hook.en: The Bogotazo broke out on April 9, 1948.

examples.es: El Bogotazo estalló el 9 de abril de 1948.
examples.en: The Bogotazo broke out on April 9, 1948.

examples.es: La crisis se desencadenó tras el anuncio del banco.
examples.en: The crisis erupted after the bank's announcement.

examples.es: El escándalo estalló cuando se publicaron los documentos.
examples.en: The scandal broke when the documents were published.

examples.es: El anuncio desencadenó una ola de protestas.
examples.en: The announcement set off a wave of protests.

examples.es: Todo se desencadenó cuando Tomás rechazó la oferta.
examples.en: It all kicked off when Tomás turned down the offer.

rule:
Use *estallar* for a sudden, serious event that breaks out: a war, a scandal, a riot. It has no *se*: *estalló la guerra*.

*Desencadenarse* is similar, with a chain-reaction feel: *la crisis se desencadenó tras el anuncio*. Without *se*, the same verb takes an object and means "to set off": *el anuncio desencadenó una ola de protestas*.

Both usually sit in the preterite, as the moment it happened. For a gradual start, use *empezar* or *surgir*. Do not use *explotar*, which is for bombs and tempers.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the vocabulary of eventuality: verbs that name how a major event begins.

options: The war broke out in 1899.
The war ended in 1899.
The war was remembered in 1899.

readAndPick.es: La crisis se desencadenó tras el anuncio.
options: The crisis ended after the announcement.
The announcement was cancelled by the crisis.
The crisis was set off after the announcement.

readAndPick.es: El anuncio desencadenó una ola de protestas.
options: The protests set off the announcement.
The announcement set off a wave of protests.
The protests were held back by the announcement.

readAndPick.es: El escándalo estalló cuando se publicaron los documentos.
options: The documents were published after the scandal ended.
The scandal was forgotten when the documents came out.
The scandal broke when the documents were published.

readAndPick.es: Estallaron las protestas en toda la ciudad.
options: Protests broke out across the whole city.
Protests ended in the whole city.
The whole city banned protests.
The war was won by no one.
No war broke out.
No war ended.

When did the crisis end?

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *estalló* or *empezó*: "The Bogotazo broke out in 1948."
yourTurn.why: A sudden, serious event breaks out: *estalló*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: "The scandal broke when they published the documents."
yourTurn.answer: El escándalo estalló cuando publicaron los documentos.
accept: El escándalo estalló cuando se publicaron los documentos.
yourTurn.why: *Estalló* and the preterite *publicaron* tell two linked moments.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: "The crisis erupted after the announcement."
yourTurn.answer: La crisis se desencadenó tras el anuncio.
accept: La crisis se desencadenó después del anuncio.
yourTurn.why: *Se desencadenó* shows the crisis as a chain reaction after the announcement.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: "The announcement set off a wave of protests."
yourTurn.answer: El anuncio desencadenó una ola de protestas.
yourTurn.why: With no *se*, *desencadenó* has an object: what the announcement set off.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *Estalló una protesta en la plaza.*
accept: Estallaron unas protestas en la plaza.
Estallaron varias protestas en la plaza.
yourTurn.why: The verb agrees with the thing that breaks out, so *estalló* becomes *estallaron*.
*No* goes before the verb, whichever order you choose.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask: "When did the crisis break out?"
yourTurn.why: The question word comes first and the preterite asks about the moment.

pitfalls.why: *Explotar* is for bombs and tempers; wars and scandals *estallan*.

pitfalls.wrong: La amistad estalló poco a poco.
pitfalls.right: La amistad surgió poco a poco.
pitfalls.why: *Estallar* is only for sudden events; slow starts use *surgir* or *empezar*.

personal: Think of a big event you remember, in your country or your family. Say how it broke out: *Estalló…* or *Se desencadenó…*
